score.intro: We froze all data on {cutoff}, predicted the {first}–{last} seasons of every field, then scored the predictions against what the satellite saw. FieldWitness is compared with {n} simpler approaches, all scored the same way.

score.mode.forecast.note: Forecast mode: what a farmer would have received on the cut-off date. The weather of the scored years was unknown, so each prediction uses the weather of past years.
score.mode.forced.note: Forced mode: the same models driven with the real weather of the scored years. It tests whether the model is right given the weather.
score.mae_median.note: average distance from the median prediction, in the measure's unit (days for dates); lower is better
score.gradeValidity.heading: Evidence grade empirical validity
score.gradeValidity.intro: Pre-registered test (cut-off 31 Dec 2021; DECISIONS.md): do higher evidence grades predict greater forecast accuracy on out-of-sample seasons (2022–2024)?
score.gradeValidity.verdict: We could not show that evidence grades predict accuracy (n = 463 field-seasons): grade-B fields had lower average error than grade-D (CRPS 17.0 vs 24.0), but the difference is within the uncertainty (95% CI of the difference −3.3 to 14.3). Grade D had only 25 field-seasons.
score.gradeValidity.verdictDetail: Pre-registered primary test: difference (Grade D − Grade B) = 7.07 with 95% spatial block bootstrap CI [-3.28, 14.32] spanning zero. Pre-registered verdict: not shown.
score.gradeValidity.bDesc: Grade B (Physics + own past calibration, 2 witnesses)
score.gradeValidity.primaryRule: Primary pre-registered test: difference (Grade D − Grade B) = 7.07 (95% spatial block bootstrap CI: [-3.28, 14.32], 1,000 resamples across 10 km blocks).
score.gradeValidity.credNote: Exploratory rank correlation between cut-off credibility score and forecast error was weak (Spearman rho = -0.033, p = 0.497). Following pre-registration, 0 grades or thresholds were altered based on these results.

explain.label: What is this? {title}
explain.evapotranspiration.title: Evapotranspiration (water use)
explain.evapotranspiration.body: Evapotranspiration is the water a field loses to the air: evaporation from the soil surface plus transpiration from the crop. The two happen at the same time and are hard to tell apart, so they are computed together. FieldWitness computes it from NASA POWER weather with the FAO-56 method.
explain.soil_moisture_anomaly.title: Soil-moisture anomaly
explain.soil_moisture_anomaly.body: NASA's SMAP mission monitors soil moisture from space; FieldWitness uses its root-zone estimate. The anomaly is the difference from the usual value for the same month: below zero means drier than usual. A shortage of soil moisture is what defines agricultural drought.
explain.ndvi.title: NDVI (greenness)
explain.ndvi.body: NDVI is computed from the visible and near-infrared light that plants reflect: NDVI = (NIR − VIS) / (NIR + VIS). Values of 0.1 and below mean bare ground; 0.8–0.9 means the densest green leaves. FieldWitness reads it from NASA HLS satellite images at 30 m.
explain.frost.title: Frost risk
explain.frost.body: Frost damage happens when ice forms inside the plant tissue and injures the cells: it is the ice, not the cold alone, that harms the plant. The calendar shows the share of past years in which the daily minimum temperature fell below the crop's threshold in that month.
explain.frost.source: Snyder & de Melo-Abreu (2005), Frost Protection, Vol. 1, Chapter 4 (FAO)
explain.water_balance.title: Water balance
explain.water_balance.body: The water balance tracks the water in the root zone day by day: rain and irrigation fill it, crop water use and drainage empty it. When the shortage passes the readily available water, the crop is stressed and uses less water. FieldWitness uses the FAO-56 root-zone water balance.
explain.ryi.title: Relative Yield Index
explain.ryi.body: The Relative Yield Index compares the expected yield with the yield the same crop would give without water shortage, on a 0–1 scale (1 = no loss). It uses the crop's yield response factor Ky, which describes how relative yield falls when crop water use falls short. It is not a yield in tonnes.
explain.ryi.source: FAO-56 (Allen et al. 1998), Chapter 8, Table 24 (from FAO Paper 33)
explain.evidence_grade.title: Evidence grade
explain.evidence_grade.body: A: physics and neighbouring fields agree, this field's past makes the physics credible, and no key input is an assumption. B: two witnesses agree. C: only one witness, or the witnesses disagree; D: most inputs that drive the decision are assumptions.
explain.evidence_grade.source: FieldWitness grading rules (config/grading.yaml); the thresholds are team choices, not taken from a paper
explain.source_tags.title: Source letters
explain.source_tags.body: Every number carries a letter: O = observed by satellite, D = derived by a model from satellite data, E = external data not from NASA, A = assumption. Point at a letter to see its exact source.
explain.source_tags.source: FieldWitness data rules (every number shown carries a source tag)
explain.nitrogen_fixing.title: Nitrogen-fixing crops
explain.nitrogen_fixing.body: Pulses take nitrogen from the air through biological nitrogen fixation and turn it into a form plants can use. FAO reports that pulses get over 60 % of their nitrogen this way, and promotes growing them in rotation with staple crops to enrich the soil.
explain.nitrogen_fixing.source: FAO newsroom, "Pulses and soils: a dynamic duo" (5 Feb 2024)
explain.cover_crop.title: Cover crops and ground cover
explain.cover_crop.body: Cover crops are grown in fallow periods, between the harvest of one crop and the planting of the next, using the moisture left in the soil. They protect the soil while it would otherwise be bare, including against the impact of raindrops.
explain.deep_rooting.title: Deep-rooting crops
explain.deep_rooting.body: Deep-rooting crops reach water stored lower in the soil. In the FAO-56 water balance, the water a crop can draw on grows with its rooting depth (Eq. 82), and Table 22 lists rooting depths for common crops.
explain.drought_tolerant.title: Drought tolerance and bad years
explain.drought_tolerant.body: Here a crop counts as more drought-tolerant when its yield response factor Ky is lower: its relative yield falls less when water runs short. Ky values are crop specific and may vary over the growing season. Bad-year numbers are the average of the worst 10 % of simulated weather years.
explain.root_zone_soil_water.title: Root-zone soil water
explain.root_zone_soil_water.body: The depth of water stored in the soil profile currently accessible to crop roots, expressed in millimeters. It increases when precipitation or irrigation infiltrates the ground and decreases as the crop transpires or water evaporates from the soil surface. When root-zone water falls below readily available thresholds, crop growth slows from water stress.
explain.root_zone_soil_water.source: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56, Chapter 8
explain.available_water_capacity.title: Total available water (TAW)
explain.available_water_capacity.body: The total amount of water that a soil profile can store between field capacity and wilting point within the crop root zone. It depends on soil physical texture across sand, silt, and clay fractions and deepens over the season as root depth expands. Soils with higher available water capacity buffer crops longer against dry spells between rain events.
explain.available_water_capacity.source: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56, Chapter 8
explain.water_stress_ks.title: Water stress coefficient (Ks)
explain.water_stress_ks.body: A dimensionless transpiration reduction factor between 0.00 and 1.00 calculated directly from daily root-zone soil water depletion. When available water remains above the crop depletion threshold, Ks equals 1.00 and transpiration proceeds without restriction. As soil dries past this threshold, Ks drops toward zero, causing modeled canopy greenness and water use to fade.
explain.water_stress_ks.source: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56, Chapter 8
explain.canopy_proxy.title: Canopy proxy (Kc / Kc max)
explain.canopy_proxy.body: The ratio of the crop basal crop coefficient Kc to its peak mid-season coefficient Kc max, scaled between 0.00 and 1.00. It is a simulation output tracing phenological leaf area progression across growth stages, not a direct satellite photo measurement. In the 3D scene, this proxy scales the height and density of procedural plant models.
explain.canopy_proxy.source: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56, Chapter 6
explain.fallow_bare_soil.title: Fallow and bare soil
explain.fallow_bare_soil.body: A fallow period leaves the field unplanted between cash crops, meaning no crop transpires and plant canopy stays at zero. While fallow conserves some moisture for subsequent planting, extended bare-soil months expose the surface to wind erosion, moisture evaporation, and organic matter loss. FieldWitness tracks bare-soil months and applies penalties to discourage uninterrupted fallow.
explain.fallow_bare_soil.source: FAO Conservation Agriculture: Soil organic cover
explain.hindcast.title: Hindcast evaluation
explain.hindcast.body: An empirical evaluation where past seasons are simulated using only data available before planting commenced. It tests model skill against actual historical satellite vegetation trajectories without looking ahead. Kansas hindcast results show honest weak skill and underdispersed intervals, while outperforming uncalibrated baselines.
explain.crps.title: Continuous Ranked Probability Score (CRPS)
explain.crps.body: A standard probabilistic verification metric measuring the distance between a predicted probability distribution and an observed outcome. Lower values indicate better probabilistic accuracy, with 0 representing a perfect probabilistic match. FieldWitness uses CRPS to evaluate whether ensemble simulations capture true crop canopy trajectories.
explain.credibility.title: Credibility score
explain.credibility.body: A composite confidence metric assessing whether local data supports a field simulation. It checks satellite observation density, model-observation agreement, and environmental plausibility. Fields with low credibility are flagged or capped at lower evidence grades.
explain.witness.title: Witness system
explain.witness.body: The three-way verification framework in FieldWitness: physics simulation (Witness 1), past field history (Witness 2), and causal neighbour contrasts (Witness 3). When all three agree, evidence confidence is high. In the current Kansas pilot, Witness 3 is kept strictly OFF because no neighbour contrast passed causal balance diagnostics.
explain.bare_soil_months.title: Bare-soil months
explain.bare_soil_months.body: The cumulative number of months in a multi-year rotation where ground cover remains below protective thresholds. Extended bare soil leaves agricultural land vulnerable to wind erosion, organic matter depletion, and evaporation. The ranking engine penalizes excessive bare-soil months to favor soil-conserving rotations.
explain.bare_soil_months.source: FAO Conservation Agriculture: Soil organic cover
explain.bad_year_water.title: Bad-year water use
explain.bad_year_water.body: The modeled crop evapotranspiration during the driest historical weather year in the field record. It reveals how severely water demand and stress escalate when precipitation fails. Adjusting the bad-year water priority slider favors crop rotations that remain resilient under drought.

methods.heading: Methods and data
methods.demo: This copy of the app runs on synthetic demo data. The methods below describe how real field packs are made.
methods.how.1: Physics: a FAO-56 root-zone water balance, driven by NASA POWER weather, simulates each rotation option on this field.
methods.how.2: Own past: the field's HLS satellite history (30 m, from 2013) calibrates the physics and gives a credibility score.
methods.how.3: Neighbours: similar fields that already grew a crop act as natural experiments for the effect of the previous crop.
methods.how.4: Agreement between the three witnesses sets an evidence grade from A to D; the options are ranked by your priorities and limits.
methods.how.5: Every recommendation is a prediction. The hindcast froze all data on 31 Dec 2021, predicted 2022–2024 and scored the predictions against what the satellite saw, next to simpler baselines (see the scoreboard).
methods.not.1: It does not predict yield in tonnes. It shows a Relative Yield Index from 0 to 1.
methods.not.2: It does not measure soil fertility from space.
methods.not.3: It does not forecast prices or profit.
methods.not.4: No language model makes the decision; the ranking is computed from the numbers shown.
methods.not.5: Weather what-ifs are sensitivity tests on past weather, not climate projections.
methods.limits.1: Coarse data (POWER weather, SMAP, GRACE, SoilGrids) is regional context or model input only. Field-level statements use HLS at 30 m from interior pixels; a source is flagged as coarse when one pixel is larger than a quarter of the field.
methods.limits.2: Field boundaries come from recent editions (CSB 2017–2024, Fields of the World 2024–25) that use imagery from after the hindcast cut-off. They are used as geometry only: no later crop labels or outcomes enter the hindcast.
methods.limits.3: Season detection from satellite achieved 78.3 % accuracy in Kansas (188 of 240 field-seasons matched USDA CSB), missing the pre-registered 90.0 % target (results/story/ks_seasons_test.json).
methods.limits.4: Neighbour witness is turned OFF: 0 of 92 primary contrasts and 0 of 32 matched contrasts passed all diagnostic checks (results/neighbours/diagnostics.md, results/neighbours/matching_diagnostics.md) due to structural rotational confounding. Because Witness 3 is inactive as an automated AI safety circuit breaker, evidence grades top out at B.
methods.limits.5: Hindcast predictive skill is weak: on 2022–2024 seasons (cut-off 2021-12-31), 90 % interval coverage is only 35.0 % for canopy integral (Spearman rank correlation rho = 0.264) and 9.0 % for cover days. Uncertainty intervals are underconfident and should be read with caution.
methods.limits.6: Grading thresholds are team choices, marked as assumptions (A), and every change is logged in DECISIONS.md.
methods.limits.7: We could not show that evidence grades predict accuracy (n = 463 field-seasons): grade-B fields had lower average error than grade-D (CRPS 17.0 vs 24.0), but the difference is within the uncertainty (95% CI of the difference −3.3 to 14.3). Grade D had only 25 field-seasons.
methods.limits.8: Baseline comparisons exclude winter wheat (no baseline run) and fallow (not scored). FieldWitness beats baselines B1 and B2 overall and for maize, but does not strictly beat baselines for sorghum (95% CI spans 0). Winter wheat displays a peak timing offset of about 36 days late (proposed explanation, not tested: phenology prior stage lengths require calibration).
methods.soil.heading: Independent soil check (USDA SSURGO)
methods.soil.intro: We compared the soil water the simulation uses with an independent survey: USDA SSURGO soil maps, read at the centre of each of the 200 Kansas pilot fields (198 had a value). Both are expressed as millimetres of plant-available water over the same 0–135 cm root zone (maize roots, FAO-56 Table 22). This is a check only; no model input was changed. The result is negative.
methods.soil.1: The simulation holds about half the water SSURGO reports. Simulation median 142 mm vs SSURGO median 282 mm; mean difference −119 mm (median −128 mm), mean absolute difference 122 mm, n = 198. Over 0–100 cm the gap is smaller but still −49 mm.
methods.soil.2: Field-to-field differences do not match: Pearson r = −0.09, Spearman rho = −0.12. The fitted water capacity per field does not follow the soil survey (note that SSURGO itself varies little here: 80 % of fields lie between 230 and 295 mm).
methods.soil.3: Why: the water balance starts from a fixed 150 mm placeholder (A) for every field, not from SoilGrids. That placeholder is 116 mm below SSURGO on average. A smaller water store means more simulated water stress, so water-stress and bad-year water numbers may be too pessimistic for these deep silt-loam soils (not tested).
methods.soil.4: SoilGrids texture vs SSURGO over the same depth: sand agrees moderately (r = 0.65, mean difference −0.7 points, MAE 7.2), clay weakly (r = 0.32, SoilGrids +6.0 points higher on average, MAE 6.3). Two fields had no SSURGO value: their soil profile ends at 91–102 cm, above the root zone.
methods.soil.source: Source: USDA-NRCS SSURGO via Soil Data Access (tag E), 11 Nov 2026. Script scripts/check_ssurgo.py; full results in results/validation/soil_ssurgo_check.md.
methods.builder.heading: Rotation Builder and Farm view
methods.builder.intro: In Field in 3D you can build a three-season rotation and watch it grow next to the current one on an illustrated farm. It changes no recommendation, grade or number.
methods.builder.1: Only the field's 36 ranked rotations can be built (the ranking's rules: at least one harvested crop, no two non-crop seasons in a row, at most two seasons of one plant family). A disabled crop card says which rule it breaks.
methods.builder.2: The table (water use, bad-year water, bare-soil months, evidence grade) comes from the ranking in the field pack, over all weather years. The 3D replay is the same FAO-56 water balance as the 3D packs, re-run in your browser for one median-rain year in normal, dry or hot weather; it matched the Python model within 0.00001 mm (20 fields × 36 rotations × 3 weathers).
methods.builder.3: The farm is an illustration of simulated values, not a photo. The barn, trees, pond, fences and paths are scenery, not data. Soil X-ray shows the same week as the glass soil view.
methods.builder.4: Limits: a season the model does not simulate (for example perennial forage in the field's history) is shown as "not simulated"; cover-crop weeks are recognised from the canopy proxy; the 3D replay is one weather year, not a forecast; it was tested with software rendering, not on every phone.
methods.wrong.heading: What we got wrong (and what changed)
methods.wrong.1: 2026-11-04 — Season detection missed target: Achieved 78.3 % accuracy on held-out test data (188/240 field-seasons; 74.6 % in pilot checks), falling short of the pre-registered 90.0 % accuracy target. Preserved openly as an honest limitation (results/story/ks_seasons_test.json, DECISIONS.md).
methods.wrong.2: 2026-11-05 — Neighbour witness failed all diagnostics: Causal Double Machine Learning on previous-crop contrasts failed covariate balance across historical sequences and failed negative control checks (0 of 92 primary contrasts in results/neighbours/diagnostics.md, 0 of 32 in results/neighbours/matching_diagnostics.md). Kept strictly OFF in grading as an automated AI safety circuit breaker against rotational confounding; evidence grades capped at B (DECISIONS.md).
methods.wrong.3: 2026-11-06 — Ranking rewarded fallow: Early ranking iterations scored bare fallow as optimal because it consumed zero crop transpiration, ignoring soil degradation. Fixed by introducing bare-soil month penalties and crop diversity constraints (config/ranking.yaml, DECISIONS.md).
methods.wrong.4: 2026-11-07 — Rank-order bug in packs and mis-tracked T6.8 metrics: In commit ce69ebf, packs had rank indices assigned prior to constraint filtering, and manual audit revealed T6.8 metric counts were tracked from intermediate script output. Corrected and covered with automated pack assertions (commit ce69ebf, DECISIONS.md).
methods.wrong.5: 2026-11-04 — Broken DOIs in data documentation: Automated link validation detected malformed and unreachable DOI URLs in early drafts of DATA.md. Replaced with verified persistent identifiers from official NASA DAAC and ISRIC registries (DATA.md, DECISIONS.md).
methods.wrong.6: 2026-11-04 — Invented datasets removed: Early AI exploration proposed using POLARIS and SSURGO soil endpoints that were unverified. Enforced strict working agreements to purge unverified datasets, standardizing solely on ISRIC SoilGrids 2.0 (DECISIONS.md Gate 0).
methods.wrong.7: 2026-11-09 — Circularity trap avoided in grade validity: Evaluating whether evidence grades predicted accuracy using current grades (derived with 2022–2024 data) would have caused outcome leakage. Caught during pre-registration and strictly evaluated against cut-off grades frozen as_of(2021-12-31) (DECISIONS.md, commit e021f3e).
methods.wrong.8: 2026-11-09 — Reconciled grade counts between pages: Grade B field-seasons differed between grade validity (n = 170) and diagnostic breakdowns (n = 97) because exploratory diagnostics dropped rows without baseline runs. Fixed to evaluate the full cohort across all pages (results/hindcast/diagnosis.md, scripts/t7_diagnosis.py).
methods.wrong.9: 2026-11-09 — Performance regression measured, not assumed: Adding 3D simulation and guided tour caused initial Lighthouse desktop score to drop from 88 to 31 (LCP 9.7 s). Instead of assuming test machine jitter, performance tracing identified eager bundle imports; resolved via dynamic code-splitting (commit 0662f39, DECISIONS.md).
methods.roadmap.gates: Before expanding to new areas, FieldWitness tests three strict validation gates:
methods.roadmap.gate.1: 1. Census & scale gate: Field size and interior-pixel share (>= 4 interior 30 m pixels with a 15 m buffer) to prevent mixed-boundary pixel pollution.
methods.roadmap.gate.2: 2. Season detection gate: Target was 90 % accuracy against ground data. Kansas achieved 78.3 % on held-out test data (188/240 field-seasons), missing the target.
methods.roadmap.gate.3: 3. Hindcast skill gate: Weak hindcast skill across fields (canopy integral 90 % coverage was 35.0 %, cover days 9.0 %, Spearman rank correlation rho = 0.264). Kansas is therefore published as a pilot with limits shown, not a general product; neighbour witness is OFF; grades top out at B; and we make no yield hindcast claims.
methods.roadmap.privacy: Privacy & data protection: Farm locations and management practices are sensitive. In version 0 ('Add my field'), all data is stored strictly on your local device. Nothing is uploaded to any server. A future server pipeline would process and store data only with explicit user consent.
methods.roadmap.future.1: Arabic interface (i18n / RTL) for regional accessibility.
methods.roadmap.future.2: Compare two fields side by side to evaluate rotations, water demand, and evidence grades across parcels.
methods.roadmap.future.3: Independent root-zone soil water and precipitation cross-checks using NASA SMAP and GPM.
methods.roadmap.future.4: Evapotranspiration cross-checks using NASA ECOSTRESS thermal data and irrigation diversion checks against Kansas WIMAS.
methods.roadmap.future.5: Expanding coverage tile-by-tile to further agricultural regions once the pre-registered validation gates pass.

methods.repo.text: The pipeline, tests, validation results and this app are public:
corr.heading: Correct this field's history
corr.intro: Tell us what you know. Your entries are ground data from you (tag E, farmer-entered). They are saved in this browser only.
corr.compare: Current rotation: satellite version and your version
corr.rerun: Re-run needed: available in live mode. The numbers in the table still describe the satellite version.
corr.nostorage: This browser blocks storage, so your corrections will not be kept after you close the page.

addfield.intro: Enter your field details to find nearest evidence. Data is kept on your device only.

addfield.check.help: Enter coordinates, pick a preset, or click on the map. Supported area is verified against the satellite tile footprint.

addfield.unsupported.error: We apologize, but this location is not currently supported.

addfield.soil.heading: Soil Test Values (Optional)

sim3d.slowFallback: The 3D view ran slowly on this device (about {fps} frames per second), so we switched to the 2D charts. Press "3D View" to try it again.
sim3d.defaultNotice: Showing top option under default priorities ({name}) — your top-ranked option is not in the precomputed 3D simulation.

tour.label: Try-it tour
tour.todo: Try it now, or press Next to move on.
tour.noTarget: The control for this step is not on this page. Use the menus above, or press Next.
tour.field.title: Pick a field
tour.field.body: Tap any field on the map or in the field list. In this Kansas pilot, evidence grades reach B at best, because the neighbour witness is turned off.
tour.season.title: Read its field story
tour.season.body: Field story shows what the satellites saw, season by season. Choose a season in the "Show" menu above the greenness chart. Season detection matched USDA crop labels in 78.3 % of field seasons, short of our 90 % target.
tour.priority.title: Move one priority
tour.priority.body: Open the Options tab and move one slider under "What matters most to you?". The ranking and the summary sentence above the table change straight away. Your priorities are saved in this browser only.
tour.why.title: Why this ranking?
tour.why.body: Scroll to "Why this ranking?" below the options table. For each criterion it shows weight × normalised value, and how much it adds to the gap between #1 and #2.
tour.sim3d.title: Field in 3D
tour.sim3d.body: Open the Field in 3D tab, press Play, then choose a −20 % rain scenario such as "Severe heat & drought". It is an illustration of simulated values — not a photo, and not a forecast.
tour.builder.title: Build your own rotation
tour.builder.body: In Field in 3D, press "Build your own rotation", drag a crop into a season (or tap it) and press Grow. Only rotations this field was ranked on can be built; the table compares yours with the current and the top-ranked rotation.
tour.limits.title: Read the limits
tour.limits.body: Open the Scoreboard and scroll to "Evidence grade empirical validity". The verdict is plain: we could not show that evidence grades predict accuracy (n = 463 field-seasons).
tour.addfield.title: Try a place outside the pilot
tour.addfield.body: In Add my field, press the Cairo preset first: it is outside the pilot, so the app says the location is not supported. Then press Garden City, which lies inside the Kansas tile (HLS T14SLH).
tour.check.builder-place: Put a crop in a season
chat.title: FieldWitness Assistant
chat.welcome: Hello! Ask me how FieldWitness works: the three witnesses, evidence grades A–D, soil water, winter wheat, the honest limits, or the field you have open. I explain the evidence; I do not make the rotation decision.
chat.input.label: Ask FieldWitness a question
chat.input.general: Ask about witnesses, grades, soil, limits…
chat.label.llm: AI-generated from project facts, may be wrong. Not a recommendation.
chat.privacy: Typed questions (and the summary of the pilot field you have open) go to a third-party AI service (Google Gemini or Groq) through our proxy. Free tiers may use data to improve their products. Do not type personal information. Fields you add yourself are never sent.
chat.note.offline: You are offline, so this answer comes from the built-in project facts.
chat.note.busy: The free AI service is busy, so this answer comes from the built-in project facts. Try again in about {s} seconds.
chat.note.unavailable: The AI service is not available right now, so this answer comes from the built-in project facts.
chat.note.guardrail: The AI reply mentioned yield mass, money or certainty, which FieldWitness never claims, so it was replaced with the built-in answer.
chat.advanced.warning: Optional. Your key stays in this browser only (localStorage) and is sent straight to the endpoint you enter. Anyone using this browser can read it. Leave this off unless you know you need it.
chat.advanced.enable: Use my own OpenAI-compatible endpoint and key
